items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — the call opened 'Hi, this is Jules. How can I help you today?' and went straight into an item-by-item inventory with no roadmap and no timeframe set. The customer never knew how long this would take or what was coming.
Never asked 'how are you today?' — 'How can I help you today' is a routing question, not a warm-up.

Home size never captured. The customer volunteered 'that's two stories at the origination point' and Jules answered 'Got it. Okay.' — no bedroom count, no square footage, and no follow-up on how many of those 60 bins are upstairs.

Stairs at origin never priced or discussed as a variable. He confirmed the storage end ('Ten by thirty is it on the first floor?') but the two-story origin — the single biggest time driver on a 60-bin carry — was acknowledged and dropped.
Never asked about additional rooms (garage, attic, outdoor storage) or special considerations — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns, stair width.
No access questions at either end: no parking, no truck access at 1400 Justin Rd, no gate code or facility hours for a storage drop, no HOA restrictions.

Never asked about additional stops. The customer raised it himself after the booking was closed — 'there's another warehouse a self-storage that's nearby. We may make a stop there' — and Jules said 'Yeah, no problem' without saying a second stop adds time and cost to the 4–6 hour estimate he had just quoted.
Moving stressors never asked — no version of 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' on a job where the customer's belongings are going into long-term storage.
No 'pricing is super simple' framing — the pricing block opened 'okay, what this is about everything that I need to get you like an estimate for your move, so. Basically we just charge by the hour.'

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. 'Insurance' was named once as a line item inside the included list ('includes the gas, the truck taxes and insurance') with no dollar figure and no explanation — on a move where 60 bins and a two-story carry go into a storage unit, this was the differentiator the call needed most.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — and the customer handed him the opening directly. Jules said 'right now we cannot guarantee exactly what time would be arriving but it's gonna be anywhere between that time' and the customer replied 'Understood.' That was the exact moment for the On-Time Guarantee and it went by unused.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees.

'No deposit required' never said. Worse, the only deposit language in the call was a charge: '$14 per moving blanket which is 100 percent refundable.' The customer left the call having heard the word deposit only in the context of paying one.
Walk distance, drive time, and traffic never named as estimate variables, despite a Highland Village origin, a Justin Rd storage destination, and a Monday 11:00–1:00 arrival window in DFW.

Entire Save Your Ass section missing. No 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill,' no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close. This was the highest-ROI section available on this call — 60 bins, a partial-contents move, and three days of lead time before Monday.

No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask. The only reply instruction was narrow — 'you can just reply to the email I'm gonna send with the additional stop.'
No closing 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the mid-call 'Do you have any questions about that so far?' covered pricing only, and the call ended on logistics.
Hours and how to reach us never given. 'You can either give us a call back this weekend' implies weekend coverage without stating hours or a number.
Customer's name used once in the whole call ('Have a great day bill') — short of the 3+ standard.
Audibility problem cost time and confidence: the customer had to ask twice on the same question — 'I'm sorry.' then 'Voice, what did you ask about?' — before Jules repeated 'How about couches?'

No rapport moment anywhere in 9.5 minutes; the inventory ran as a rapid checklist ('How about beds?' 'How about couches?' 'Any outdoor furniture?') with almost no acknowledgment of the customer's answers.
top_strength: The clock and the close. Jules delivered the clock section completely and cleanly — 'the price starts once we arrive at your house and then we have, you would have. As for as long as you need us, we have a minimum of two and a half hours and then after that we prorate every fifteen minutes. Does that make sense' — all four bullets including the sense-check, which is the section most reps skip entirely. He then made his pricing concrete instead of abstract: 'if we're only moving these items I would estimate that the move could take anywhere from four to six hours... for example, it us four hours it's gonna be $816 in case it'll take us six hours it's gonna be $1,224 but then again you only pay after the move is completed with the actual time use for the move.' Naming both ends of the range in dollars, then anchoring the floor at '$510,' is exactly the budget-conscious framing the rubric asks for. He also asked for the business and adapted when pushed back on — offered Monday 8:30–9, and when the customer asked 'Do you have anything in the afternoon on Monday?' he checked rather than deflecting, came back with the 11:00–1:00 window, set expectations honestly about the arrival window, and closed: 'I will book this move for you right now and then I'll send over the confirmation email and we're gonna see you on Monday afternoon.' A quoted job booked inside 9.5 minutes on the first call is the outcome the scorecard exists to produce.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: the Save Your Ass speech, which was 100% absent on the one call type where it pays most. This customer has roughly 60 bins already packed in a two-story house and three days before Monday. Jules should have said, 'Bill, one thing that saves you real money — every minute the guys spend walking is billable, so anything you can move downstairs and stage near the front door before Monday cuts straight off your bill. If you can get the bins from upstairs down to the garage or entryway, and take the small stuff — loose items in drawers, anything breakable — in your own car over the weekend, you could easily be at four hours instead of six. That is a $400 difference. Does that make sense?' That single paragraph is worth more to the estimate-accuracy rock than anything else on this call, because it moves the actual move time toward the low end of the range he just quoted. Second priority: the missed differentiator pair. Jules said out loud 'right now we cannot guarantee exactly what time would be arriving' — the correct line is 'and here is the good news, we back that window with our On-Time Guarantee. If we miss it, we start discounting your move immediately.' And with everything going into storage, the No Worries pitch was mandatory: 'You are also covered by our No Worries Damage Coverage — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage, and there is no deposit to hold Monday.' Three sentences, three rubric bullets, and the only deposit the customer hears about stops being the blanket charge. Business risk to fix in EMMA today: the customer disclosed a likely second storage stop after the booking closed and was told 'no problem' with no time or cost caveat, so the 4–6 hour / $816–$1,224 estimate he agreed to does not include that stop. Get a note on the job now and follow up for the address before Monday, or this books as an estimate miss and a day-of surprise. Also missing from the record: origin bedroom count and stair count, and whether the 60 bins are upstairs — load-planning gaps on a job with only two movers assigned.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient, patient and genuinely warm at the close ('My pleasure. Have a great day bill'), but the middle of the call ran as a clipped inventory checklist with almost no acknowledgment of the customer's answers, the name was used once, and there was no rapport or humor moment anywhere in 9.5 minutes.
audio_review_reason: The customer twice could not make out the same question ('I'm sorry.' / 'Voice, what did you ask about?' before Jules repeated 'How about couches?'), and several stretches of the transcript are garbled on both sides ('Bolt build Davidson', 'there's no monsters'), so speaking volume, clarity and pace cannot be judged fairly from text — the Bonus clarity point was scored against him and should be confirmed on audio.
